messages.subject: Data Table Interaction
parts: Is there a simple demo showing how to choose an item in a data table and then perform a task? I would like to click on an item in a cell and then plot data associated with it elsewhere in my app.

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Data Table Interaction
parts:
The basic idea can be simple, but a decent user interface is harder to
design and requires much more thinking. Below is a simple demo of
obtaining the row/column indices when you click on the table:

library(shiny)
library(DT)
cellCallback = JS("
table.on('click', 'td', function() {
Shiny.onInputChange('foo_cell', table.cell(this).index());
});
")
shinyApp(
ui = fluidPage(fluidRow(
column(8, DT::dataTableOutput('foo')),
column(4, verbatimTextOutput('info'))
)),
server = function(input, output) {
output$foo = DT::renderDataTable({
datatable(iris, callback = cellCallback)
})
output$info = renderPrint(input$foo_cell)
}
)

There are a number of things to consider:

1. JavaScript indexes from 0 instead of 1 (see Section 2.2 for more
info: http://rstudio.github.io/DT/);
2. Whether you want some visual feedback from clicking the cell, e.g.
a blue outline or something like that;
3. How to preserve the selected cells during pagination, sorting, and
searching, or whether you want to preserve them at all;
4. Whether you want to select multiple cells.

I think #3 is the major challenge. I have not thought well about this
problem, so I have not exposed such cell-level info to users in DT
yet. Ideas and comments are welcome.

Regards,
Yihui
